signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + Crowded Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.74, holding just below the 160.00 threshold that historically triggers BoJ verbal warnings. Reports of a Saudi oil tanker being halted in the southern Strait of Hormuz corridor introduce a geopolitical risk premium, though VIX at 14.9 indicates broad cross-asset stress remains contained for now. The 266bp Fed-BoJ OIS carry differential (SOFR 3.64% vs TONA 0.98%) continues to anchor the pair's upside bias despite a strong options put skew (25d RR -1.74), which suggests institutional hedging against a sharp reversal. JPY COT LF net short of -81,619 (pctl 9) confirms the carry trade remains crowded, leaving the pair vulnerable to a disorderly unwind if geopolitical tensions escalate significantly. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry advantage persists while VIX remains below 25. Catalyst: Next BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias priced. Risk: Break above 160.00 triggers confirmed MoF intervention, forcing a liquidation of spec shorts.

signals.title: AUD/USD — COT Extreme + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD is trading at 0.7168, maintaining its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7110/0.7019/0.6975). Speculative positioning is heavily crowded, with COT LF net long at +53,578, reaching the 95th percentile of its 52-week range (z +1.92). This institutional length is met by an extreme retail short of 88%, creating a sharp divergence that often precedes a late-trend exhaustion. While the 71bp OIS carry premium (AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.64%) supports AUD, the massive +8.8% Vol Risk Premium (IV 14.7% vs HV30 6.0%) indicates the options market is paying a significant premium for protection against a realized vol spike. Trade bias: Neutral AUD/USD; crowded spec longs and high vol premium suggest limited further upside. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — 0% hike priced. Risk: Retail capitulation and a break above recent highs targets a fresh spec add.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Bearish Positioning + Dovish USD Headlines
signals.text: EUR/USD sits at 1.1621, trading above its SMA20 (1.1599) but remaining capped by the SMA200 at 1.1637. COT data shows an extreme positioning shift, with LF net short at -55,311 (pctl 3, z -2.28) after a massive WoW delta of -55,635. This extreme bearishness faces immediate headwinds from TIER-1 headlines following dovish comments from Scott Bessent and the market's consolidation after Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech. While the 145bp USD carry advantage (SOFR 3.64% vs ESTR 2.19%) remains the structural driver, the negative USD ESI (-9.7) and the extreme spec short in EUR suggest the pair is primed for a short-squeeze if US data continues to underperform. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/USD; contrarian squeeze potential against extreme spec shorts. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep — hike bias priced. Risk: ECB signals a dovish shift, aligning policy with the crowded spec short and removing the squeeze incentive.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Technical Support + Real Rate Advantage
signals.text: GBP/USD is holding at 1.3550, successfully defending the SMA20/50/200 cluster localized between 1.3430 and 1.3546. Speculative positioning is highly concentrated with LF net long +56,839 (pctl 96, z +1.58), but the 1M 25d RR remains relatively neutral at -0.25, suggesting a lack of urgent downside hedging in the options market. The UK real policy rate of +0.35% provides a restrictive backdrop compared to the JPY and CHF accommodative regimes, helping sustain the Pound's resilience despite a negative ESI (-9.2). The current bear-steepener regime in US yields typically supports the USD, but the SONIA-SOFR spread at -9bp keeps the carry differential effectively neutral. Trade bias: Long GBP/USD; supported by moving average cluster and real rate advantage. Catalyst: Next BoE meeting — hold bias priced. Risk: A close below the SMA200 at 1.3441 invalidates the bullish technical structure.
